ITO films with thickness between ~200 and ~700 nm, sputter-deposited at room temperature on both glass and plastic substrate, are polycrystaline with a cubic structure, with crystallite sizes between ~10 and ~30 nm and lattice distortion between ~0.5 and ~0.2%.

ITO coatings deposited at room temperature on PET substrates are polycrystalls, with crystallite sizes increasing and lattice distortion and free carrier concentration decreasing when the coating thickness is increased.

a detailed investigation of the influence of the film thickness in the properties of ITO films grown on glass or PET substrates at room temperature.
the influence of the ITO film thickness on the structural, electrical and optical properties, which are relevant in the design of optoelectronic devices, such as organic solar cells.
the optimization of ITO coatings for applications in flexible devices, where the substrate is a PET foil.

the film thickness has a strong influence on the structure, electrical, optical and mechanical properties of ITO films grown at room temperature.

the ITO coatings deposited on PET by sputtering have the same structure and optical properties as those deposited on glass, but with a slightly lower lattice distortion and higher carrier concentration.
the film thickness has a significant effect on the structure, the optical and the electrical properties of ITo films deposited at room temperature.

the film thickness plays an important role in determining the properties of ITO layers deposited by sputter at room temperature on both glass and plastic substrat
ITO layers with high transparency and conductivity can be obtained by sputtering, even at room temperature, provided that the film thickness is optimized.
, the film thickness is the main factor that influences the structure, optical, and electrical properties of sputtered ITO films, while the substrate material is a minor factor.

, by controlling the film thickness, ITO coatings can be obtained with good optical and electrical properties at room temperature on plastic substrates.
